text:
kiran: FYI running into a weird SSE parse failure in sampleapp-web. Repro when the client reconnects immediately after an auth-refresh: sometimes the parser gets a leading NUL (\u0000) or stray byte before the next event's '{' and JSON.parse blows up. Seen on Chrome + our fetch-based SDK behind envoy in staging.

evan: NUL? can you paste raw capture (curl -v -N or hexdump) + SDK/version?

kiran: sdk@0.9.4, sampleapp-web. Minimal curl from staging (tokens redacted):

```\n$ curl -v -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer <x>" "https://staging.redwood.io/stream/.."\n> GET /stream/.. HTTP/1.1\n< HTTP/1.1 200 OK\n< Content-Type: text/event-stream\n< Transfer-Encoding: chunked\n:\n: keepalive\ndata: {"id":"100","t":1}\n\n\r\n\x00{"id":"101","t":2}\n\n\n```\n
kiran: note the literal 0x00 inserted before the next JSON chunk. Our parser currently treats any non-empty leading characters as continuation and attempts to JSON.parse the concatenation.

sara: interesting. Could be envoy or TLS terminator injecting a 0x00 as a padding/marker when connections are torn down and re-established. Do we use HTTP/1.1 vs HTTP/2 for the route? Also does the SDK keep a partial buffer across abort?

kiran: we keep a partial buffer. current parse logic: append incoming chunk to buffer, split on "\n\n", then for each event split lines and accumulate lines starting with 'data:'; finally JSON.parse on the joined data. No CRLF normalization and we don't trim non-printables.

evan: two vulnerability points: 1) arbitrary non-printable bytes at chunk boundary, 2) partial buffer surviving abort+reconnect. Fix proposals: normalize CRLF -> LF, strip leading non-printable chars (\u0000..\u001f) before attempting JSON.parse, and on abort clear the partial buffer synchronously. Also instrument a metric when we see non-printable repair attempts.

sara: agree on conservative repair + metric. Another idea: on reconnect pass Last-Event-ID header and ask server to dedupe; but that's server-side change. For client: when JSON.parse fails, if trimmedCandidate = candidate.replace(/^[\x00-\x1F]+/, '') differs, try JSON.parse(trimmedCandidate) once and emit metric 'sse.parse_repair'. Don't hide the error if it still fails.

kiran: implemented a quick patch locally: buffer = buffer.replace(/\r\n/g, "\n"); on abort partial = ''; when parsing do a quick trim of leading non-printables before JSON.parse. On a 20k-iteration flapper test failure rate dropped from ~3.2% -> 0.12%.

evan: good. But let's avoid normalizing too aggressively and masking server bugs; metric will help. Also check envoy config: 'stream_idle_timeout', 'use_remote_address', and any buffer limits; some proxies add null-byte padding when switching connections to preserve chunk alignment. I can spin up an envoy with identical config and run tcpdump to confirm.

sara: add unit tests simulating: (a) \r\n split across chunks, (b) leading NUL before JSON, (c) abort+fast reconnect. Also add an integration test in sampleapp that toggles a short token TTL to force auth-refresh.

kiran: opened PR fix/sse-nonprint-trim with tests + metric hook. CI: build-bot: running checks...

build-bot: CI passed for branch fix/sse-nonprint-trim (checks: 11/11) :white_check_mark:

evan: after merge, backport to 0.9.x patch release and add a short troubleshooting note in sampleapp README explaining how to curl -v -N and look for stray 00 bytes or CRLFs between chunks. Also file a follow-up to audit envoy/edge for any middlebox injecting padding.

sara: small UX note: update JS SDK docs to recommend consumers guard JSON.parse (try/catch) when using raw stream events, and point them to our SDK config flag 'sse.repairOnNonprint=true' that we'll include behind a feature flag for one release.

kiran: will monitor metric after deploy; will open follow-up if repair rate >0.1% or if envoy study shows insertion on our side. gist with minimal repro + hexdump: https://gist.github.com/redwood/devex-sse-nonprint (private). Thanks team!
